facts.value: next normal pay period or 14 days after dismissal, whichever occurs last
facts.summary: Kentucky: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due next normal pay period or 14 days after dismissal, whichever occurs last.
facts.evidence_quote: Any employee who leaves or is discharged from his employment shall be paid in full all wages or salary earned by him; not later than the next normal pay period following the date of dismissal or voluntary leaving or fourteen (14) days following such date of dismissal or voluntary leaving whichever last occurs.

facts.value: next normal pay period or 14 days after leaving, whichever occurs last
facts.summary: Kentucky: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due next normal pay period or 14 days after leaving, whichever occurs last.
facts.evidence_quote: Any employee who leaves or is discharged from his employment shall be paid in full all wages or salary earned by him; not later than the next normal pay period following the date of dismissal or voluntary leaving or fourteen (14) days following such date of dismissal or voluntary leaving whichever last occurs.

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Kentucky basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $7.25.
facts.evidence_quote: Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $7.25 Premium Pay After Designated Hours 1 : Weekly - 40, 7th day The 7th day overtime law, which is separate from the minimum wage law, requires employers who permit covered employees to work seven days in any one workweek to pay the employee at a rate of time and one-half for hours worked on the seventh day when employees work all seven days of the workweek. The 7th day overtime law does not apply when the employee is not permitted to work over 40 hours total in the workweek. The state adopts the federal minimum wage rate by reference if the federal rate is gre
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.value: KRS 405.435(2) requires employers to report new hire information to the SDNH within 20 calendar days of hiring and/or re-hiring an individual who resides and/or works in Kentucky.
facts.summary: Kentucky new hire reporting timeframe (per OCSE): KRS 405.435(2) requires employers to report new hire information to the SDNH within 20 calendar days of hiring and/or re-hiring an individual who resides and/or works in Kentucky.
facts.evidence_quote: Reporting Timeframe: KRS 405.435(2) requires employers to report new hire information to the SDNH within 20 calendar days of hiring and/or re-hiring an individual who resides and/or works in Kentucky.
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)

facts.notes: Federal floor is 20 days; states may set shorter deadlines. Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.
